dedupe_keys.name: epa national stormwater calculator swc with green infrastructure cost module

description: The National Stormwater Calculator is a web application that estimates the annual rainfall runoff and the frequency of runoff from a site in the United States, including Puerto Rico, under different development and green infrastructure scenarios, using long-term historical rainfall. It runs the EPA Storm Water Management Model (SWMM) in the background, so users do not set SWMM up themselves. Low impact development controls include rooftop disconnection, rain harvesting, rain gardens, green roofs, street planters, infiltration basins and porous pavement, and a cost module gives regional and national planning-level capital and maintenance costs based on published cost equations (a data.gov dataset gives the unit and regional cost spreadsheets). It is developed by the EPA Office of Research and Development; the mobile web app version 3.4.0 (August 2022) runs in any browser and the Windows desktop version 2.0.0.1 is no longer supported, both free with user guides. Caveats: it is a screening tool for small sites up to about 12 acres with uniform soils, it needs an internet connection, and costs are planning-level estimates. It supports site-scale green infrastructure scenario screening and cost comparison that can feed city-scale stormwater models; a related record is the International Stormwater BMP Database.
name: EPA National Stormwater Calculator (SWC) with green infrastructure cost module
notes: The International Stormwater BMP Database and SWMM records are on other branches and are named in prose only.
